topics.label: Encinar restoration · conditional models
topics.description: Estanislao de Simón Navarrete’s 1996 paper presents restoration models selected by initial vegetation, soil condition and terrain water balance. It distinguishes eroded ground, well-conserved shrub cover and degraded ground with surviving oak mats, alongside special runoff/drainage settings. Pine-assisted restoration is one conditional route; favourable microsites can allow direct oak introduction. Outcomes include oak woodland, pine woodland, mixed stands, oak scrub and broadleaf galleries. Stages describe source guidance rather than measured trials, universal succession or an approved modern field prescription. No fixed duration, irrigation amount, survival percentage or general planting density is established. The Gádor reference is a difficult establishment setting, not a demonstrated whole-mountain treatment.

topics.label: Encinar and carob heritage · funding considerations
topics.description: Curator synthesis: conserving documented native woodland, a historic vegetation mosaic, a significant old carob tree or associated knowledge can be investigated within environmental and landscape heritage. A restoration design must document the actual asset, habitat suitability, purpose, public benefit, rights and applicable professional evidence. The AL20 strategy links cultural/natural heritage with soil regeneration. Existing operation types 3.1, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 offer different kinds of work to examine, subject to their own conditions. Under 3.5, agricultural-production support and forestry productivity are excluded; required forest planning and public-use/dissemination conditions remain separate checks. Under 3.4, novelty and nonproductive demonstration requirements also apply. Neither native status nor a source paper proves eligibility, available funding, selection points or an award.

topics.label: Environmental and geological heritage
topics.description: Natural heritage includes biological and geological resources with relevant environmental, landscape, scientific or cultural value. The Spanish law distinguishes natural/seminatural habitats, species habitats, landscape and ecosystem restoration. Native habitats, ecological corridors, wetlands, significant trees or geological features are possible investigation subjects; a site assessment must establish the actual values and pressures. These are explanatory examples, not a designation of the user’s land or automatic LEADER eligibility. The AL20 EDLL explicitly includes natural heritage within NPL3 and assigns it a separate OE3.3 monitoring indicator. Its diagnostic response supports conservation and land-stewardship initiatives, and its intervention-logic table connects soil regeneration and erosion/aridity reduction to the heritage objective. These are source-stated strategic links; they do not classify every parcel or supply an approved restoration or planting plan. Explorer examples now connect encinar vegetation and conditional restoration models with the Gádor woodland/mining context, and distinguish the genetic/cultural value of particular old carob trees and cultivars. Open the anchored heritage branch for ecological references and conditional funding considerations. These examples require local asset evidence; native status and modern planting alone do not establish recognition or eligibility.

topics.label: GEA Sierra de Gádor reforestation 2018–19 · Project
topics.description: GEA’s 2018–19 volunteer campaign aimed to restore native woodland in northeastern Sierra de Gádor. Its updated report describes four sowing days at La Zarba and Aljibe del Marqués: over 5,000 encina/coscoja acorns across over 2.5 ha beneath previously thinned Aleppo pine. Seeds came mainly from Sierra de Segura. The stated technique used two or three acorns per prepared spot, often already germinated, taking advantage of shelter and soil moisture. The report also records earlier plantings since the 1990s, better-developed plantings receiving care/irrigation, and scarce saplings from a failed administrative planting. These are implementer observations and planting inputs, not a controlled trial or survival census. Long-term survival and funding status remain unreported.
